REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON YOUTH ORDERS
To The Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
Your Commi ttee on Youth Orders has been active this year in an effort
to promote healthy, active support of our Masonic Youth on the part of
our Lodges and the individual Masons. Several meetings of the Commi ttee
have been held, each in a different section of the State to allow attenda nce
by those in that general area without undue expense.
It is evident to this Commi ttee that we as Masons are not giving to these
fine organiz ations the support which they need and deserve. They are, in
many cases, ultimate ly depende nt on the Masonic Organiz ation, through
its Lodges and through its individual member s, for their ongoing wellbeing. Too often, in the past, we have been made to feel it is our duty to
support the Youth because we owe it to them for their sake. The truth is,
we need them more than they need us.
The major needs of the Youth Groups , in so far as Masonic support is
concern ed, continu e to be an adequat e number of good adult leaders and
the conside ration of our Lodges in keeping the cost of rent for meeting in
our buildings at a minimu m. The staffing of their adult leadersh ip position s
with good, compet ent Masons is a problem to be solved by exposur e and
educatio n. The dedicati on necessary to fill those positions must come from
the heart and not the head. As far as rent is concern ed, surveys routinel y
show that when a compar ison of rents paid by the various Organiz ations
meeting in a Masonic Temple on a cost per membe r per meeting basis is
made, our Youth Groups are paying a higher rent than the Lodge. When
we are charging our young people more for the privilege of meeting in our
building than we pay ourselve s, somethi ng is wrong!
This Commi ttee has underta ken a general program of educatio n as one
of its major projects this year. With the blessing of Most Worshipful Robert
0. West and the hospitality of Right Worshipful Joe Hammo nd, Grand

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

Lecturer, and the Ritual Committee, a few moments on the agenda of
each of the Division Ritual Conferences was devoted to emphasis on the
Youth Orders. The adult head of one of our State Youth Organizations
was invited to speak to the assembled Grand Lodge Officers and District
Inspectors at each Division Conference. These were well received in every
case. The Grand Master ended these presentations with a plea for each
District Inspector to make time in one of his District meetings for a similar
presentation by a knowledgeable Youth Order worker. Many of the Inspectors accommodated that request and invited such a program into their
Districts. However, for the most part that plea was not honored and thus,
many of our Lodge Officers were not exposed to the direct conversation
of the needs of our Youth Groups.
Again this year, Grand Master Robert 0. West issued a request for each
Worshipful Master to appoint a Youth Coordinator in his Lodge in an
effort to help this Committee develop a network of interested Masons
throughout the State with representation by every Lodge. Again, a few of
our Lodges have complied but many have not. This Committee's Chairman
has recommended that next year the Committee be staffed with fewer
members, placing further emphasis on the need for each Lodge to have a
Coordinator to assist in carrying out the purposes of the Committee for
the benefit of our Masonic Youth.
Another major project of the Committee this year was that of making
available to each Worshipful Master a flyer suitable for mailing to every
member of his Lodge in his Trestleboard, encouraging that member to
submit names of prospective members for any of the three Youth Orders.
Somewhat fewer than half of our Lodges took advantage of this offer
resulting in approximately 95,000 of the flyers being distributed. This resulted in the receipt of 118 flyers with a total of prospective members'
names as follows:

Specific thanks is given to Grand Secretary Robert Klinger and his efficient staff for their many acts of support and assistance throughout the
year. The Chairman is also most appreciative of the many tireless acts and
the dedicated and efficient service performed on behalf of each of the
Committee members.
Brethren, we urge your interest in and support for our Youth and the
effort of this Committee. Remember, "Be a model, not a critic."

AFTERNOON SESSION-Wednesday, October 13, 1982
At 1:30 P.M. Grand Lodge was called on, the Grand Master presiding.
This session of Grand Lodge was raised by Perry E. Olsen, Master of
Pajaro Lodge No. 110, Maynard M. Beall, Master of Hesperian Lodge
No. 264, Harold D. Norton, Master of Table Mountain Lodge No. 124 and
David L. Jones, Master of Clear Lake Lodge No. 183. The gavel used for
the raising of Grand Lodge was presented to the Grand Master at the East
Bay Masters and Wardens 45th Annual Spring Breakfast in Oakland. Other
gavels used during the Afternoon Session were presented to the Grand
Master at a reception by Ionic Lodge No. 520 in Los Angeles, at the
Cornerstone Laying Ceremony of West Hills Community College Educational Facility in Lemoore, hosted by Welcome Lodge No. 255 and Coalinga Lodge No. 387, at the Institution of Half Moon Bay Lodge U. D. in
Half Moon Bay and the 125th Anniversary and Hiram Award at Table
Mountain Lodge No. 124 in Paradise.
The Very Reverend Lawrence J. Osborne, Grand Chaplain, delivered
the Afternoon Prayer.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON FINANCE
To The Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
Audited financial statements for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1982,
have been received from the Grand Treasurer and reveal that costs for the
operation of our Grand Lodge again rose more than twelve percent (12%)
or, about the same increase as was experienced last year. We commend
the Grand Master for his many personal efforts to control costs of this
Communication and other events throughout the year. Committee Chairmen also are worthy of your praise as they operated well within budgeting
limits.
Your Committee on Finance operated this past year under the new,
enlarged charter which the Grand Lodge approved at last year's Annual
Communication. New procedures were established for the review and approval of all expense claims and the Committee involvement in other financial areas of the Grand Lodge reflected the broader scope of responsibility envisioned by the revised charter.
Supplementary appropriations for those items where budgets were exceeded totaled $51,228.00 and we're duly approved by the Grand Master.
It is estimated that publication and distribution costs of the California
Freemason Magazine for the 1982-83 year will be approximately $180,000,
and we are therefore including a per capita assessment increase of $ .15 to
cover the additional costs of our official magazine of the Grand Lodge.
For purposes of reimbursing Grand Lodge Officers, staff, Committeemen, Inspectors, etc. for use of their personal cars on Grand Lodge busi-

INSTALLATION OF OFFICERS
At 5:00 P.M. the Installation Ceremony commenced, with the retiring
Grand Master, Most Worshipful Robert 0. West, acting as Installing Officer, and Past Grand Master Vernon L. Gordon acting as Master of Ceremonies. In accordance with Ritual, all of the Appointive Officers were
duly installed after which the Grand Lecturer, Grand Secretary and Grand
Treasurer were installed. The Junior Grand Warden and Senior Grand
Warden were then invested with the Arthur S. Crites lapel pins and appropriately installed in their respective stations. The Deputy Grand Master
was presented with the lapel pin of his office and installed after which th.e
Grand Master was duly installed. Grand Master Maynard expressed his
appreciation to the installing "team" and invited each of the Elective Officers to introduce those members of their families who were in attendance.
The newly installed Grand Master then requested the Grand M~rshal
to present the wife of the Junior Past Grand Master, Jean West, m the
East and called upon the former Grand Orator, Melville H. Nahin, who
eloq~ently presented her with a gift on behalf of the entire membership
of the Fraternity. This material gift was accompanied with the love and
best wishes of our great Fraternity. This charming lady then graciously
responded in expressing her appreciation. Carolyn Maynard, the wife of
Grand Master Maynard, was escorted to the East and presented with a
beautiful bouquet of roses for which she appropriately expressed her thanks.

263

Past Grand Master Vernon L. Gordon presented to the Junior Past Grand
Master, the Past Grand Master's apron. Past Grand Master Raymond A.
Ebbage then presented the Past Grand Master's lapel pin to the retiring
Grand Master, following which he was presented with the Past Grand
~aster's Certificate by Past Grand Master Kermit A. Jacobson. The newly
mstalled Grand Master, Harry L. Maynard, presented the Junior Past Grand
M~stcr Robert 0. West with a Past Grand Master's ring. Each presentation
which was made expressed the appreciation of the Masons of this Jurisdiction for the contributions made to the Fraternity by the retiring Grand
Master.
The Grand Master introduced the Administrators from the Homes, their
ladies and the Homes' residents who were in attendance. The Brethren
and their ladies from Hawaii were asked to stand for recognition. John G.
Chase, Master of San Buenaventura Lodge No. 214 and Samuel L. Hill
Master of Poinsettia Lodge No. 633 were also introduced. Over two bus~
loads of friends and fellow employees of Grand Master Maynard from
Ventura were asked to stand for recognition, following which members of
his family were introduced. His charming daughter Linda approached the
East and presented a gavel and sounding block with the inscription "Hold
High the Torch of Freemasonry, with love from Carolyn and Linda."
Grand Master Maynard then addressed the assembled Brethren and
gues~s .. He exp.ressed his thanks to those in attendance for being with him
at his mstalla~ion. He also expressed his appreciation for the friendship
extended to him from all of the Past Grand Masters. Their guidance and
assistance is greatly appreciated. He will look forward to the promotion
and enlargement of the success of Layman's Night; Masonic Widows Programs and Hiram Recognition Award programs. Activities outside of the
Lodge Room will be encouraged, and with God's help, your new Grand
Master will carry the torch of life for Freemasonry.
At the conclusion of the Grand Master's installation message he was
accorded a standing ovation.
Following the Benedition by the newly installed Grand Chaplain, the
Very Reverend Sidney S. Guthman, the assembled guests retired for a
reception to greet the newly installed Grand Lodge Officers.
All business of the 133rd Annual Communication was completed at 6:35
P.M. after which the newly installed Grand Master announced that Grand
Lodge would be called on at 9:00 A.M. on Thursday, October 14, 1982
for the purpose of closing.

THURSDAY MORNING, October i4, 1982
~t 9:0? A.M. Gr~nd Lodge was called on for the purpose of closing.
This session was raised by Albert G. Cowan, Junior Warden of North
Hollywood Lodge No. 542. The gavel used was the one presented to the
Grand Master by his wife and daughter at his Installation Ceremony on
Wednesday.

NOTE 1 - SUMK4.RY Of SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES:

NOTE 1 - SUMK4.RY CF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES:

282

The financial statements of Masonic Homes of California have been
Significant accounting
prepared on the accrual basis of accounting.
policies follow:
fund Accounting:
To insure observance of limitations and restrictions placed on
t.he use of resources available to the Homes, the accounts of the
Homes are maintained in accordance with the principles of fund
accounting.
The assets, liabilities and fund balances of the Homes are
reported in four self-balancing funds, as follow:
General fund - Resources are available to support the operations
of the Homes at Union City and Covina, California.
Permanent Endowment fund - Ordinances of the Grand Lodge provide
that no portion of the principal of the Permanent Endowment fund
shall be expended for any purpose and income from the principal
shall be used only for the maintenance and general operation of
Masonic Homes.
Hugo M. Lorber Masonic Home, Union City fund - This fund provides
for the operation, preservation and betterment of the Home at
Union City, California.
Restricted Trust funds - Details to this Trust fund are contained
in Note 8 to the financial statements.
Land, Buildings and Equipment:
Land is reported at cost. Buildings and equipment existing at
June 30, 1982 and June 30, 1981 are reported at cost or at
depreciated replacement cost as determined by independent appraisors
(see Note 2).

283

(Concluded)

Depreciation is recorded by the straight-line method over the
following estimated lives:
Buildings and improvenients
Equipment
furniture and fixtures
Vehicles

2 - 55 years
7 - 12 years
10 - 20 years
2 - 7 years

Maintenance and repairs are charged to expense when incurred.
Betterments of a major nature which extend the useful lives of
buildings and equipment are capitalized: · on sale or retirement, the
cost and accumulated depreciation applicable thereto are eliminated
from the accounts and the differences between net book value and the
proceeds -from sale or retirment are included in income.
Other Assets:
Other assets consist of life insurance policies, real estate and
mineral rights assigned or bequeathed to the Masonic Homes.
Real estate and mineral rights are recorded at the nominal value
Payments by the Masonic Homes of
of $1 each for accountability.
obligatio"5 of the assignors secured by these assets are added to the
nominal value.
Life insurance policies are recorded at their actuarily determined present values.
NOTE 2 - PRIOR PERIOD ADJUSTMENTS:
In the previous year financial state111ents, the balance sheet and
statement of support, revenue and expenses and· changes in fund balances
were restated as of June 30, 1979 and 1980 to give effect to a change in
accounting method which recognized depreciation. In addition, the cost
of buildings and equipment at June 30, 1980 and 1981 were restated to
give effect to depreciated replaee111ent costs at Union City, as determined
by independent appraisers.
During the current fiscal year~ the financial statements at June 30,
1981 and year then ended have been restated to give effect to depreciated
replacement costs at Covina, as determined by the independent appraisers.
